subject: Finex vendor bake-off: recap, open questions, and next-step testing plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Green <samantha.green@finex.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@finex.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Finex vendor bake-off: recap, open questions, and next-step testing plan

Hi Samantha / Raj —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap so we have alignment and a concrete set of next steps you can share internally. I kept this tight to preserve what we agreed and call out the three highest-priority evaluation axes for your team (latency, cost, and hallucination risk).

What we heard (pain / goals)
- Peak web UI latency target: 300ms p95 for 1k qps baseline (important for user conversion).
- Backend batch throughput for nightly indexing: need predictable cost below $X per 100M tokens.
- Security / audit: VPC requirement + audit logs retention for 12 months.
- Output quality: financial summarization accuracy > 95% on your gold set; low hallucination on entity extraction.

Competitive context you mentioned
- You’re running a three-way bake-off: Redwood Inference, CloudFlowAI, and GigaServe. Current focus is: interactive latencies during peak and hallucination behavior on Finex prompts.

Open questions we agreed to validate in the next tests (owners and timeline)
1) p95 latency under 1k qps with 512-token context — owner: Redwood (Jordan) — run by 2026-03-02 EOD. (Attachment: latency-run-0228.log template)
2) Gold-set quality evaluation against your sample prompts (95% threshold) — owner: Finex (Samantha / Raj) + Redwood to re-run on our side — deliverables: CSV of per-prompt scores and failure modes by 2026-03-04. (Attachment: sample-prompts-and-gold.json)
3) Cost projection with realistic mix (chat + embedding + rerank) — owner: Redwood (Lauren) — deliverable: cost sheet and sensitivity analysis by 2026-03-03. (Attachment: redwood-bakeoff-matrix.xlsx)
4) Security checklist items: VPC networking steps and audit-log retention proof — owner: Finex (security team) + Redwood to provide KMS/KV details — target: 2026-03-06.

Proposed short-run tests we recommended on the call
- 10-minute sustained 1k qps latency test (p95 target) with your typical prompt mix.
- Focused hallucination test: 50 prompts from gold set that historically failed on other vendors.
- Cost sensitivity: 3 scenarios (baseline, optimized batching, quantized model variant).

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-matrix.xlsx (pricing/cost model), sample-prompts-and-gold.json, latency-run-0228.log

Next meetings
- Check-in demo with results: Tuesday 2026-03-03 11:00am PT (proposed) — 30 minutes.

If that matches your notes, please confirm and we’ll schedule the test window for Monday (3/1) and share the exact test harness steps.

Thanks,
Jordan

Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 08:10:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: quick vendor delta and suggested test knobs

Jordan / Rachel —

Following the Finex call, I sketched a compact vendor comparison and a set of adjustable test knobs we should expose in the harness. Key diffs for the bake-off: 

1) Latency profile- Redwood: consistent low p95 with prefix caching + continuous batching; strong for tail with smaller contexts.
- CloudFlowAI: slightly better single-request latency in small-scale tests but degrades more at sustained qps due to queueing.
- GigaServe: optimized for throughput but higher p95 at low concurrency.

2) Cost and quantization support- Redwood: recommendations available for int8/quant variants, easy fallbacks.
- CloudFlowAI: cheaper list prices but less guidance for quality tradeoffs.
- GigaServe: good throughput with specialized hardware (proprietary) — pricing not transparent.

3) Security & private deployment- Redwood: full Private deployment with customer KMS + audit logs; need to map exact network steps for Finex VPC.
- CloudFlowAI: supports VPC peering but customer-managed keys are limited.
- GigaServe: more limited controls on audit retention.

Suggested test knobs for the harness (we should provide the toggles in the test plan):
- token_limit: 256 / 512 / 1,024
- concurrency: 400 / 1,000 / 1,500 qps
- batching: aggressive / default / disabled
- model_variant: high-accuracy / balanced-quant / quantized-lowcost
- seed_prompts: full gold set / 50-critical / random-sample-200

Action items for Redwood before Monday runs:
- Finalize harness and test-run script (Jordan) — by EOD 2026-03-01.
- Prepare cost sensitivity workbook (Lauren) — by 2026-03-03.
- Assemble KMS/private deployment tech note (Rachel) — by 2026-03-04.

I attached the skeleton bake-off matrix I’ll upload to the Drive.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop | Solutions Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
